answer: Distinct Inlet Registration. Each agent registers through a randomly assigned network inlet; the registry samples cross-inlet traffic to confirm a vertex of independent origins, not a clique. Duplicate inlets collapse into one identity. Attackers must rent and continuously exercise many real, distinct network paths, paying per-path bandwidth plus a velvet holding deposit that is forfeited if two identities trace to one inlet. Cost scales with the number of independent origins, not with claimed accounts.
